label: models/fw_walllamp.mdl: a caged wall lamp with a sodium-orange glass

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_gaussammo.mdl, models/w_silencer.mdl, models/w_crossbow_clip.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked C, B, D, D where the asset was A, B, D, C: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: Outline matches a caged wall lamp in all ten views: a flat back plate against the wall (back and right views), a cage of bars around a rounded orange glass, and a hood on top. Nothing sticks out or is missing. The hood overhangs the cage evenly in the left, right and front-left views.

M2.reason: The brief gives no size for the lamp, so there was no size to hold it to. The measure is 14 x 14 x 18 with sizeAsked null and sizeOff null, so the 15% check could not be made. Not clearly off, but not verified either.

M3.reason: Parts the brief asks for, down to the small ones: a cage (the bars around the glass, a cross-shaped frame in the front view and a lattice in the side and front-left views), the sodium-orange glass (a rounded dome, seen in front, below and top views), and a wall mount (the flat back plate). A hood and a small bottom tab are also there. The brief asks for no rivets, claws, teeth, handles or round-part sides, so none is missing.

M4.reason: The glass is sodium-orange as the brief asks. The back plate and hood are a painted green-grey metal, which sits with the brief's green-grey palette, and the cage is dark steel. The brief names no other colour for the lamp, so nothing is off.

M5.reason: The glow is there: the orange glass has a lit, streaked pattern in the front and below views. The brief asks for an industrial, worn look, but the green plate and hood are smooth and mottled with no rust, scuffs or wear marks, and the cage is plain black. Wear is missing where the brief asks for it.

M6.reason: Line-up test: judges picked the asset as the one not made by Valve in 2 of 4 readings (asset at B and at D were caught, at A and C they picked other models). That is under the three-of-four catch threshold, so the test does not cap M6. Beside the other three, the lamp reads as a game prop.

M7.reason: The front (the cage face with the glass) faces out. The back plate is flat and upright against the wall, and the lamp stands on its mount with nothing tilted or lying. The brief gives no origin to check against.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors. At 116 triangles it is under the 194 that Half-Life's most complex kind of prop spends (median 56), so it is not over the bound. Nothing is open or inside out: the back plate is solid, the cage bars are closed, and the glass is whole behind them. Nothing that a player can see is missing.
